messages:
alex_w: Silverline POC - seeing sudden 503s + intermittent 401 token errors during ramp. Started ~10:45 PT after we increased concurrency to 12 per route. High priority, engineering oncall please. Logs attached.

maya_se: On it. Do we have request ids or example traces? Are they using dedicated or hosted? @ishaan_oncall?

alex_w: They're on hosted with default routing to r1-small. Example curl and raw response:

alex_w: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-silverline" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-3b","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"service_unavailable","request_id":"rq_01F8X2...","note":"no healthy downstream"}
```

ishaan_oncall: I can see matching request IDs in the infra logs, rolling errors from 10:44:12. Looking at router logs, there's a surge of 502/503 due to backend oom/killed pods on dedup-worker pool. Posting snippet:

ishaan_oncall: ```
2026-03-20T17:44:12Z router-1 INFO request rq_01F8X2... routed -> backend dedup-3
2026-03-20T17:44:12Z dedup-3 ERROR oom-kill pid=3245 rss=6.2G
2026-03-20T17:44:12Z router-1 ERROR 503 returned to client rq_01F8X2...
```

maya_se: Are they ramping token length? any long context? Also seeing 401s in auth-service logs for the same client key, says 'invalid_jwt' around same time.

nina_sec: Checked token signing keys, no rotate in last 24h. Could be their client rotating tokens mid-session; confirm with Silverline.

james_a: Silverline contact (Tom) says they started parallelizing inference workers and are using short-lived tokens from their IAM. He pasted their side logs: "token_exchange succeeded -> next req 401". Sounds like clock skew or caching issue.

ishaan_oncall: Potentially two issues: (1) their workers cause backend OOMs -> 503s. (2) token bounce due to replay/caching or signing key mismatch -> 401s. For immediate mitigation I can:
- throttle concurrency for Silverline at the routing layer to 4
- route to an autoscaled pool with larger VMs (r2-large) to reduce OOMs
- add circuit-breaker fallback to older model variant
I'll run throttling now unless someone objects.

maya_se: Do it. Also add a canary route to r2-large and increase cache TTL for auth validation to 60s as a stopgap.

ishaan_oncall: Executing:
ishaan_oncall: ```
# throttle
ctl route update --client silverline --concurrency 4
# create canary
ctl route create --client silverline --pool r2-large --weight 10 --note "canary for POC"
# auth cache
kubectl -n auth patch configmap auth-cache --patch '{"ttl":60}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by ishaan_oncall for route updates (deploy id: dpl_7738)

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded in 25s (dpl_7738)

alex_w: Throttle + canary in place. Tom from Silverline confirms 503s dropped immediately but a few 401s persist.

nina_sec: For the 401s, suggest we inspect auth-service logs for 'kid' mismatch and their token issuer time. If they are rotating keys, they need to publish JWKs or allow small TTL.

maya_se: I called Tom, he says their token microservice rotates keys every 30s (!) for security. That's too fast. Suggested they slow to 5m or publish the JWK endpoint with a stable kid. I've put it as a blocker for go-live.

james_a: Pricing/security question from finance side: if we need to migrate them to dedicated r2-large for stability, what's delta? Need estimate for sales. (cc @maya_se)

maya_se: I'll loop in account exec for pricing. For now SRE recommends keeping on hosted with throttles and canary until commit. If they want guaranteed throughput we propose a Dedicated reserved pool.

ishaan_oncall: Action items:
- SRE: monitor for 1h, keep throttle
- Sec: work with Silverline on JWK publish & token TTL
- Sales: estimate cost delta for dedicated r2-large reserve
- Eng: investigate root cause of OOM on dedup-worker pool

alex_w: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread as war-room. Next check-in at +30m (1993054500). If anything urgent DM.

maya_se: noted. ping me if 401s don't drop after JWK fix.

ishaan_oncall: Monitoring dashboards: https://dashboards.internal/r/silverline-poc

alex_w: Update @1993054500: 503s back to baseline, 401s largely resolved after Silverline slowed token rotation and we extended auth cache TTL. Silverline to evaluate for Dedicated. Closing war-room but leaving throttle for now. :white_check_mark:
